item.title: Archbishop Wood falls to Scranton Prep in state football opener
item.description: SCRANTON — Archbishop Wood fell behind early and couldn't recover as impressive Scranton Prep, the PIAA District Two Class 3A champs, rolled to a 49-7 win over the Vikings in a first-round state playoff game Friday night. The loss ended the season for the District 12-champion Vikings (9-4) while the Cavaliers (12-1), winners of 12-straight games, advanced and will face Wyomissing Area in next week's quarterfinals. Scranton Prep, which has scored 150 total points in its three postseason games, scored on all five of its first-half possessions and led 35-0 at intermission. More: Wood tops Carroll for PCL title Archbishop Wood thumps Archbishop Carroll in PCL 3A football title game What’s next for Archbishop Wood football? The loss ended the season for the Vikings . What’s next for Scranton Prep football? The Cavaliers will play District Three champion Wyomissing Area in the PIAA Class 3A quarterfinals next week. Key play It came on the game's first possession when Scranton Prep junior quarterback Owen Jeffers fumbled a high snap, but was able to corral it and complete an 8-yard pass for a first down to senior Ricky Dewey. One play later, Jeffers found Dewey for a 21-yard touchdown. By the numbers 5 - possessions for Scranton Prep in the first half that produced five touchdowns and a 35-0 lead at halftime, which meant a mercy rule and a running clock in the second half. 7, 7 - passes thrown by Jeffers in the first half and passes completed by Jeffers, to go along with three touchdown tosses. He finished the game with four touchdown throws. Drew Markol covers local sports for PhillyBurbs.com . Support our journalism with a subscription. item.title: If this is the end, it’s a disappointing one
item.description: If Puka Nacua has played his final game as a member of the Los Angeles Rams, it’s a disappointing end for fans. Nacua elected to have what seems to be season-ending surgery to repair his knee injury in a contract year . The Rams will likely regret not extending his contract before the year started, as his lack of long-term security likely factored into the business decision. If Nacua had future assurances, he might have put off surgery in order to make a comeback towards the late regular season into the playoffs. And to make matters worse, Nacua suffered said injury on a meaningless play. Sean McVay called a receiver run to salt away an insurmountable lead against the Washington Commanders. It didn’t make sense at the time. It felt even worse once the injury news broke. Somehow, it seems even more nonsensical now. Puka Nacua was a generational draft steal Nacua’s production through his first four NFL seasons—when healthy—rivals that of former top draft picks in Odell Beckham, Justin Jefferson, and Ja’Marr Chase. The key difference: Nacua was the Rams’ third draft pick in the fifth round back in 2023. He went on to record the most yards by a rookie receiver and he’s second to only Jefferson through three seasons. This is the kind of found money that should set a franchise up for years. Instead, the Rams might have wasted their opportunity. Despite what looks to be a large amount of available salary cap space heading into next offseason, Los Angeles has a handful of difficult decisions to make—Nacua included. They will also decide whether Kobie Turner, Byron Young, Steve Avila, Kevin Dotson, Coleman Shelton, Warren McClendon, Colby Parkinson, and others over the next couple of years. That money is reserved for taking care of their own. If they don’t, the cupboard will be left so bare that the Rams risk falling back into irrelevance. And separately there is the issue of how the Rams have used Nacua. The team has failed to properly stack the receiving corps around their star pass catcher. Often times over the last few seasons it has seemed like their passing game was simply Nacua or bust. As a result, he’s handled a historically large workload. That has taken a toll on his body especially with the physical nature in which he approaches the game. That could be the reason why the Rams are hesitant to invest in Nacua long-term, which would be another sign that they failed to protect the luxury of their 2023 draft day steal. If this is the end for Nacua with the Rams, it’s an incredibly discouraging way to separate. The team has turned a historic advantage into a few years of great production with little to show for it thereafter.

item.title: Purdue basketball catches fires, burns Oakland with record performance
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Finally, Purdue basketball buried an opponent after building a big lead. The Boilermakers' three-game winning streak saw buy game opponents Illinois State, Ohio and Lipscomb rally from double digits and make things too close for comfort after Valparaiso did the same and eventually upset Purdue in double overtime. Oakland failed to do what those teams could, quiet the typically raucous Mackey Arena fans. The Boilers built a 30-point halftime lead on their way to a 95-49 victory over the Grizzlies. And they did it in record-tying fashion. Purdue broke its program record with 21 made 3-pointers, passing a mark set at Iowa in 2018 . In the final minute, it was senior walk-on Jace Rayl who made the record breaker for his first career made field goal. Along the way, Purdue got some breakout performances for new pieces of the roster who are seemingly finding their fit. Purdue basketball turning point vs. Oakland Purdue's two losses to open the season can be blamed on many things, one of those its out of character atrociousness on 3-point attempts. During it's three-game winning streak, the Boilers shot 40.5% from beyond the arc. Gicarri Harris entered Friday's game making 10 of 18 3-pointers this season. Off the bench, the junior guard quickly buried 3s on consecutive possessions, putting Purdue ahead 15-4. It was a sign of things to come. Purdue sank 9 3-pointers in the first half at a 45% clip. Oakland couldn't recover from that blitz, which only got worse in the second half. Game MVP It was only a matter of time before Luke Ertel busted out. Last year's Indiana Mr. Basketball after leading Mt. Vernon to a Class 4A state championship caught fire against Oakland. Ertel drilled 8 of 10 3-pointers, finishing with a career-high 24 points. Ertel also showed his point guard mentality with 5 assists. More: Richard Moodie, bound for Tennessee, stays focused on Purdue soccer NCAA Tournament run Three Purdue basketball standouts vs. Oakland Jack Benter: Since being inserted into the starting lineup after those two losses to start the season, Benter has impressed. That was the case again against Oakland. Benter collected 9 points, 7 assists and 4 rebounds. Caden Pierce: Pierce, a former Ivy League Player of the Year at Princeton, has settled into his role as a starting power forward. Pierce can provide mismatches there and against Oakland that showed. Pierce had 13 points on 6 of 8 shooting. Daniel Jacobsen: The 7-foot-4 center continued his early season dominance. Jacobsen made 7 of 9 shots, scoring 16 points to go with 9 rebounds, 4 blocks and 2 assists. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. item.title: Raiders’ Klint Kubiak Weighs In on Fernando Mendoza’s Biggest Mental Challenge
item.description: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders Getty Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders Getty Fernando Mendoza #15 and Kirk Cousins #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders Getty Last week, the Las Vegas Raiders officially headed into a new era for the storied NFL franchise, as the team traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings and named rookie Fernando Mendoza their starting quarterback for the foreseeable future. It was a move that was to be expected, as the Raiders view Mendoza as their future face of the franchise, but his first start did come against the defending Super Bowl champions and head coach Klint Kubiak’s former team, the Seattle Seahawks. Klint Kubiak on Fernando Mendoza’s Mindset Getty Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders Ultimately, the Raiders lost to the Seahawks, which wasn’t all that surprising with the rookie quarterback going up against one of the best defenses in the NFL. After the game, Mendoza talked about the experience, and also admitted he was too much in his own head. On Friday, ahead of Mendoza’s second start, Kubiak spoke to the media about Mendoza’s mindset and what he needs to do heading into the divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos in Week 11 at Empower Field at Mile High. “It’s just being comfortable, and I think obviously the less that you have to think about the play calls and the situations,” Kubiak said of Mendoza’s mindset. “The game just comes more and more naturally to you the more reps that you get. So he’s going in the game two, and he’ll keep getting more comfortable.” The Broncos will be another tough test for Mendoza, as it will be his first road game and his first in Denver, which is never an easy place to play, especially for the Raiders. item.title: Kyle Shanahan talks viral Mac Jones moment: ‘If you just saw it once, you’d be like who’s this corny white dude?’
item.description: Mac Jones is the moment. Despite being a backup quarterback for the 49ers, many of his teammates view him as the life of the party. Jones recently went viral for accompanying Deebo Samuel and Trent Williams during the 49ers’ popular boombox entrance. Head coach Kyle Shanahan discussed Jones’ walkout vibe, which quickly captivated social media. San Francisco 49ers quarterback Mac Jones looks on before a game against the Washington Commanders at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., Oct. 19, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Yeah I saw that. My kids sent it to me. It was awesome, but that’s how we see Mac like that every day,” Shanahan said. “If you just saw it once, you’d be like who’s this corny white dude? But you don’t at all because he is like that all the time. He is always upbeat. He is always having fun. “There really hasn’t been a day that Mac isn’t like that, which is extremely unique. That’s why he’s one of the most liked guys on our team.” Mac Jones #10 and Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers warm up before the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Getty Images San Francisco 49ers quarterback Mac Jones on the NFL Network set at the Super Bowl LX media center at the Moscone Center. Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Jones joined the 49ers in 2025 on a two-year, $7 million contract. He has been a productive backup to quarterback Brock Purdy since his arrival last season. Teams showed interest in trading for Jones at the deadline, but the 49ers ultimately retained the Alabama product. While Jones may not be a starter frequently, his presence in the locker room can’t be understated. Josh Hazlewood denies Sandpapergate knowledge and warns of Test exit if Pat Cummins is removed as captain Josh Hazlewood described Pat Cummins as a "great leader" and the fast bowler has now backed those words with a show of loyalty as he has defended the Australian Test captain against fresh claims linked to the 2018 sandpaper scandal, also insisting that he knew nothing about any plan to alter the ball. Cummins has been under heavy fire since Usman Khawaja said the entire team was aware of the plot during the Cape Town Test of 2018. David Warner and, more recently, Cameron Bancroft have made similar claims that everyone in the group knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball. Hazlewood has sided with Cummins, who has always said he took no part in the plan. The 35-year-old has taken 313 Test wickets, and in 2021 he co-signed a document along with Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, in which all four denied any prior knowledge of sandpaper being taken onto the field. Hazlewood described the criticism of his captain since Bancroft’s 4,000-word column earlier this week as “a bit of a pile on”. item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 42 - Kevin Willis (1996-98, 2001-02)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the eighth of 12 who wore the No. 42, Kevin Willis. After ending his college career at Michigan State, Willis was picked up with the 11th overall selection of the 1984 NBA Draft by the Atlanta Hawks. The Los Angeles, California native played the first 10 seasons of his pro career with Atlanta. He also played for the Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors before he joined the Houston Rockets for the first time in free agency in 1996. It ended with a trade to the Toronto Raptors in 1998. Between stints, he played for the Denver Nuggets and Milwaukee Bucks before he was dealt back to Houston in 2001, lasting until he signed with the San Antonio Spurs in 2002. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Willis wore only jersey No. 42 and put up 11.8 points and 7.4 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: LeBron James has Sixers drawing 215,000 viewers in Philadelphia market
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images LeBron James is big business, and that fact is paying off for the Philadelphia 76ers. On the court, the Sixers are off to a 13–2 start to the season — their best since 2000 — and current stand atop the Eastern Conference. But beyond their record, James’s impact on all of the business that surrounds the team may be even greater. A report from Rob Tornoe at the Philadelphia Inquirer noted that the Sixers are drawing in 215,000 viewers in the Philadelphia area per game this year on NBC Sports Philadelphia, which owns the local broadcast rights for the team. It’s a 150% increase over last season. The impact of James has been so great that it is even shaking up the local news scene in Philadelphia. According to Tonroe, while Action News at 6ABC is still the top news program in the area, NBC10 is presenting the “first serious ratings challenge” to their spot in years with help from the bump the Sixers have provided. NBC10 president and general manager Joel Davis noted that the network’s cross-promotion between its news desk and its sports team covering the Sixers has been a boon to expanding their reach. “When we run news promos in NBC Sports Philadelphia, we are getting a younger audience exposed to our news product,” Davis told Tornoe. While whatever boost LeBron provides to the team can only last as long as he keeps playing, there’s reason to believe the Sixers are set to only grow in their share of ratings from here. Usually, this part of the calendar would be mostly reserved for the Eagles in the greater Philadelphia area, but with the Birds playing like one of the worst teams in the NFL, the Sixers have been able to stake their claim on the local sports scene a bit earlier than usual. If the wins keep coming and they look like they can make a real run through the postseason, it’s possible we’re only seeing the very beginning of what the LeBron effect looks like in full. item.title: Hurricanes Readying for ‘Measuring Stick’ Game Against Oilers
item.description: Hurricanes Oilers Getty The Carolina Hurricanes are readying for a visit from the Edmonton Oilers in what one player calls a true “measuring stick” game. The Hurricanes won the Stanley Cup last season and are currently in first place in the Eastern Conference. The Oilers, meanwhile, are in second place in the Western Conference, so this could truly be a 2027 Stanley Cup preview when these two teams meet on Saturday night. ‘Measuring Stick’ Game for Oilers and Hurricanes Ahead of this clash of the titans on Saturday night, Oilers veteran Mattias Ekholm admitted that the game was a measuring stick for his team as they look to see how they stack up against the defending Stanley Cup champions. “It’s a measuring stick, they’re the top team in the League for sure. We played them not too long ago, so we know what to expect. It’s an early game on a Saturday, so I’m sure the building will be nice and loud, and we’ll look to rebound from this,” Ekholm said (via NHL.com). For Oilers forward Filip Hallander, the Hurricanes present a challenge because they are deep and have four lines that can score goals . “They have so many lines that can produce and play good. They’re a four-line team and obviously they won last year, so it’s going to be a good challenge for us,” Hallander said. Mike Babcock Knows How Good the Hurricanes Are Oilers head coach Mike Babcock, who has been around the league for a long time, knows how good this stacked Hurricanes team is. He believes they are even better than the last time the two teams met, and knows that the Oilers are going to be in for a tough game when they go against the defending champs. “They’re not trying to surprise us tomorrow and we’re not trying to surprise them. They have more guys than the last time we played them, they’re going to be a deep team. We’ve tried by moving people around to get a little deeper so we can come at you, shift after shift, after shift, and that’s our plan,” Babcock said. item.title: Tennessee takes care of Coastal Carolina, 78-51
item.description: Nov 20, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Volunteers guard Juke Harris (2) dunks the ball against the Coastal Carolina Chanticleers during the first half at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tennessee basketball was in a classic let down spot — or look ahead spot — depending on how you look at it on Friday night at Food City Center. For the Volunteers, it didn’t matter. Tennessee was coming off of a huge win over No. 2 Michigan State on Tuesday night. Although they allowed to let Coastal Carolina hang around for a few brief minutes, they quickly stomped out any upset hopes. Led by DeWayne Brown with ten quick points and six boards, Tennessee took the lead midway through the first half. Juke Harris got off to a nice start as well, hitting four of his eight shots in the opening half. The Volunteers held Coastal Carolina to just 2-16 to end the half, while Tennessee shot 10-14. That turned into a 14-2 run, which gave Tennessee control of the game going into halftime and the rest of the way. Tennessee even got freshman wing Manny Green into the action a little bit. The 6-8 guard was active, hitting a three-pointer, grabbing two steals, two boards and an assist. The Vols kept working through the post, feeding Brown as he logged another big night. The Tennessee big man ended with 20 points and 11 rebounds. Tennessee held a 20-point lead for much of the second half, cruising to win No. 5 on the year. It was a little sloppy down the stretch, but Tennessee had the clamps down defensively. Coastal couldn’t find any traction in the paint, and the Vols’ forced them into 7-33 shooting from three-point range. Terrence Hill Jr. had a light night, but was able to find seven assists in just 21 minutes of play. item.title: Packers Breakout Star Matthew Golden Receives Midseason Award
item.description: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden is having a career year in his second season, helping establish the passing attack as one of the best in the NFL. Golden is playing so well that he was voted the Breakout Player of the Year for the 2026 NFL Channel Midseason Awards . The 23-year-old wideout has struggled with drops, but is still producing at a high level. He has hauled in 58 receptions for 853 yards and five touchdowns. Golden is forming one of the best receiver tandems in the league with Christian Watson. Golden consistently gets open with a great route-running ability. He has been a reliable target for Jordan Love when he doesn't drop the ball. Love is having a great season, completing 63 percent of his passes for 2,838 yards, 20 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. If Golden can limit the drops down the stretch, he could establish himself as one of the best receivers in the NFL. The Packers' offense has struggled to establish the run game, and their offensive line has had some struggles, which is why they have leaned so heavily on Golden and the passing attack. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Golden's development has been clear, as he had a much smaller role in his rookie year, catching 29 passes for 361 yards and zero touchdowns. He is now a top target in Green Bay's offense and should continue to be a focal point down the stretch. The Packers hold a 6-4 record and need to have a strong end to the season to make it into the playoffs. They are in a battle for a spot in the postseason, with teams like the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks . Green Bay could also try to win the NFC North, but they are currently in last place, as the Chicago Bears , Detroit Lions , and Minnesota Vikings are all 7-2. Golden was one of the few bright spots on offense for the Packers in their loss to the Vikings last week, as he had five receptions for 70 yards. However, he did have a few major drops, which led to the end of drives for Green Bay. If Golden has a strong end to the season, he has the chance to be an All-Pro or a Pro Bowler. The Packers will need Golden and their entire roster to play at an elite level in the final stretch of the season to make it into the playoffs and compete for a Super Bowl.

item.title: Yankees Flagged as Potential ‘Mystery’ Team in Tarik Skubal Rumors
item.description: Tarik Skubal instagram story Getty The New York Yankees could be embarking on a quiet campaign to land top free agent prize Tarik Skubal. The star pitcher has garnered interest from several teams — and a reported $400 million offer from the crosstown New York Mets — but the Yankees have not been publicly identified yet as one of them. But one MLB insider believes the Bronx Bombers could be the still-unnamed “mystery” team that has reportedly met with Skubal this week. Yankees Could Be Pursuing Tarik Skubal MLB.com reported that Skubal has already held several on-the-books meetings with teams, along with one more secretive visit. “We know that Skubal has reportedly held meetings with the Mets, the Blue Jays, the Dodgers and the Padres this week. But there is at least one other team in the mix; we just don’t know which one,” the report noted. “MLB Network insider Jon Heyman reports in the New York Post ( subscription required ) that a fifth team met over Zoom with Skubal on Wednesday. Which team? That is undisclosed, per Heyman. But it’s possible that club and the ace left-hander could have an in-person meeting later.” While there are still no solid reports on the identity of that “mystery team” pursuing Skubal, SI.com writer Noah Camras suggested it would only be logical that the Yankees are in the mix. “The Yankees don’t need starting pitching, but have the financial muscle to sign Skubal if they wanted to,” Camras wrote. “Big-name free agents always love to have as many big-market teams pursuing them as possible. Thus, why wouldn’t the Yankees at the very least be in the running?” The Yankees have gone toe-to-toe with the Mets when chasing free agents before, losing out on Juan Soto to New York’s $765 million offer. But Camras suggested that a more logical team could be Skubal’s unnamed suitor, noting that the Detroit Tigers are open to a return, as is Skubal. Yankees Could Focus on Other Roster Needs The Yankees have already made some big moves to boost their pitching staff. Closer David Bednar accepted this one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer, while Tim Hill returned on a new one-year deal. With the moves to boost the bullpen, some insiders expect the Yankees to focus on finding a second baseman to replace Jazz Chisholm, as well as some other moves for their infield. item.title: Verstappen and Russell at war as explosive FP3 incident sparks FIA investigation
item.description: Max Verstappen and George Russell were involved in a heated confrontation during the closing stages of the third free practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix , with the two drivers making contact before the Dutchman showed his middle finger to the Mercedes driver. The incident will be investigated by the stewards after the session. The confrontation began when Verstappen overtook Russell along the Las Vegas Strip, positioning his Red Bull directly ahead of the Mercedes before beginning to weave from side to side as the two approached the braking zone. Russell responded aggressively, diving down the inside under braking in an attempt to reclaim the position. The two drivers came extremely close together and eventually made contact as the Mercedes driver forced his way back ahead. However, the confrontation did not end there. Shortly afterwards, Verstappen moved back in front of Russell and made his frustration clear by showing the British driver his middle finger. Race control subsequently noted the incident, with the stewards confirming that the encounter between the two drivers would be investigated after FP3. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen's frustrations boil over after difficult session The confrontation came at the end of an already frustrating session for the four-time world champion, who repeatedly struggled under braking throughout the hour. Despite setting the pace during the opening stages, Verstappen complained that his Red Bull felt too "sharp" and subsequently made several mistakes, running wide on at least four occasions and being forced to turn around before continuing. The incident with Russell was also the second time Verstappen attracted the attention of the stewards during FP3. Earlier in the session, the Dutchman had been involved in a potentially dangerous encounter with Franco Colapinto while weaving to warm his tyres. The Argentine approached from behind before overtaking Verstappen on the start-finish straight, only for the Red Bull driver to reclaim the position at Turn 1. That incident was also referred to the stewards for a post-session investigation. Meanwhile, Russell went on to dominate the session with a remarkable 1:34.041, finishing almost a second ahead of Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli. Verstappen eventually finished sixth, 1.309 seconds behind Russell, with two separate stewards' investigations awaiting him after the chequered flag.

item.title: Texas A&M reportedly benching Marcel Reed in favor of Brady Hart vs. Oklahoma
item.description: South Carolina linebacker Fred "JayR" Johnson (0) trips up Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed (10) during an NCAA college football game Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, in Columbia, S.C. South Carolina won 17-9. (AP Photo/Artie Walker Jr.) (Artie Walker Jr./AP Photo/Artie Walker Jr.) Texas A&M is finally going in another direction at quarterback. According to a report from On3's Pete Nakos , the Aggies are expected to bench Marcel Reed vs. Oklahoma on Saturday and give Brady Hart the start at quarterback. While the move is a big one, it's not necessarily surprising. Reed has regressed badly this season and the A&M offense has been woeful all season. He has thrown for just 1,712 yards, eight touchdowns and nine interceptions while completing just 55.7% of his passes. On the season, the A&M offense ranks 109th in total offense, 95th in scoring offense and 107th in passing offense. Hart is a sophomore and has appeared in seven games over the last couple seasons, mostly in mop-up duty. According to 247Sports, Hart was a three-star recruit out of Cocoa, Fla. and ranked as the No. 31 quarterback in the Class of 2025. He saw some action last week vs. Tennessee, completing 2 of 3 passes for 22 yards and an interception in the loss. Hart was inserted into the game after Reed started and completed 9 of 22 passes for 71 yards with a pick. It's been an ugly year for A&M, as the Aggies have followed their College Football Playoff appearance in 2025 with a disastrous 2026. A&M enters this week's game against Oklahoma with a 4-6 record and 1-6 record in conference play. The move to bench Reed comes a few days after head coach Mike Elko vehemently defended Reed following the 22-7 loss to Tennessee . "Our offense is inept," Elko said. "I don't know how you can put this on one kid. It's on me. It's a completely nonfunctional offense. Come after me." A&M and Oklahoma are set to kick off at 2:45 p.m. Saturday in Norman, Okla. The Boston Red Sox thought that a key relief pitcher made their roster when they announced that Johan Ovideo would be a part of their bullpen at the end of spring training. However, after pitching in one game in late March against the Houston Astros, the relief pitcher was placed on the Injured List with a right elbow strain, and he never made another appearance for the big-league team throughout the rest of the year. The Red Sox traded Ovideo to the Arizona Diamondbacks for Class-A lefthander Luke Dotson. The trade was reported by Bob Nightengale. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ovideo went from the 15-day injured list to the 60-day list in mid-April. He was able to make a rehab appearance for Triple-A Worcester in mid-September. Prior to coming to the Red Sox , Ovideo had been a starter with the Pittsburgh Pirates in the final two months of the 2025 season. He started 9 games with the Pirates and 3.57 earned run average and he held opposing hitters to a .182 batting average while compiling a 2-1 record in 40.1 innings. Ovideo has pitched in six Major League seasons. He pitched 2-plus seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals from 2020 through 2022, and he moved on to the Pirates and spent 2-plus years in Pittsburgh. Ovideo had his best season in 2023 when he went 9-14 while making 32 starts and pitching 177.2 innings for the Pirates. He had a 4.31 earned run average with 158 strikeouts and 83 bases on balls. He also led the National League with 13 hit batters that season. Ovideo did not pitch in 2024 because he was sidelined after undergoing Tommy John surgery. item.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
item.description: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday. In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

item.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
item.description: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality. He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session. Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . item.content:encoded: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
item.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year.
